original_question: Let T113(a,b) count tilings of the (a,b)-benzel when both stone orientations are allowed and all three bone orientations are allowed. Is the sequence T113(n, 2n-3), defined for n >= 4, 2-adically continuous as a function of n?
target_in_paper: Section 8, Problem 16: "Is T113(n, 2n−3) 2-adically continuous as a function of n ≥ 4?" This is the unweighted type-113 problem; the nearby weighted analogue is Problem 18, which uses T113(n, 2n−3; 3) instead. ([samuelfhopkins.com](https://www.samuelfhopkins.com/OPAC/files/proceedings/propp.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper's exact target: it uses the unweighted counting function T113(a,b), it identifies the correct tiling class (both stone orientations allowed and all three bone orientations allowed), it picks the correct diagonal (n, 2n−3), and it includes the same lower bound n ≥ 4 that appears in Section 8, Problem 16. ([samuelfhopkins.com](https://www.samuelfhopkins.com/OPAC/files/proceedings/propp.pdf))
missing_details: The draft should explicitly tie T113(a,b) to the paper's general notation Tijk(a,b), where i records whether right stones are allowed, j records whether left stones are allowed, and k is the number of allowed bone orientations; thus type 113 means right stones allowed, left stones allowed, and all three bone types allowed. ([samuelfhopkins.com](https://www.samuelfhopkins.com/OPAC/files/proceedings/propp.pdf))

To be fully stand-alone, the paper's definition of the (a,b)-benzel should be stated, for example via barycentric coordinates: it is the polyhex whose cell-centers are triples (i,j,k) in Z^3 with i+j+k=1 and -(a-1) ≤ j-i, k-j, i-k ≤ b-1. ([samuelfhopkins.com](https://www.samuelfhopkins.com/OPAC/files/proceedings/propp.pdf))

The phrase "2-adically continuous" should specify the topology: the integer variable n is viewed with the 2-adic metric, and the integer values T113(n,2n−3) are viewed inside the 2-adic integers with the same metric. ([samuelfhopkins.com](https://www.samuelfhopkins.com/OPAC/files/proceedings/propp.pdf))

It is worth making explicit that this is the unweighted Problem 16, not the weighted Problem 18; in the weighted version the notation is T113(a,b;3), where a tiling with m stones has weight 3^m. ([samuelfhopkins.com](https://www.samuelfhopkins.com/OPAC/files/proceedings/propp.pdf))
refined_question: Let B(a,b) be the (a,b)-benzel, i.e. the polyhex whose unit-hexagon centers are the triples (i,j,k) in Z^3 satisfying i+j+k=1 and -(a-1) ≤ j-i, k-j, i-k ≤ b-1. Let T113(a,b) denote the number of tilings of B(a,b) by the right stone, the left stone, and the three bone prototiles (vertical, rising, and falling), so that both stone orientations and all three bone orientations are allowed. For integers n ≥ 4, is the map n ↦ T113(n, 2n−3), viewed as a map from {n in Z : n ≥ 4} to Z with the 2-adic topology, 2-adically continuous? ([samuelfhopkins.com](https://www.samuelfhopkins.com/OPAC/files/proceedings/propp.pdf))
justification: The draft is targeting Section 8, Problem 16 almost verbatim. Section 1 supplies the exact notation Tijk(a,b) and identifies type 113 as the case with both stones and three bones, while Section 8 states the specific peripheral-diagonal question for T113(n,2n−3) with n ≥ 4. I did not broaden the question and I did not switch to the weighted notation, because the paper treats that separately as Problems 17 and 18. ([samuelfhopkins.com](https://www.samuelfhopkins.com/OPAC/files/proceedings/propp.pdf))
